exact_statement: The recovered bond-percolation target assumes G infinite, connected, locally finite, quasi-transitive and p_c(G)<1. Omitting p_c<1 makes the claim false: the two-sided line has p_c=1 and theta(1)=1.
assumptions: two-sided nearest-neighbor line for the counterexample
proof_or_counterexample: ATTEMPT.md section 1: each infinite ray at p<1 has probability lim_n p^n=0; at p=1 every bond is retained.
remaining_gap: Full target remains unproved here; current literature status UNKNOWN.

exact_statement: On any countable connected locally finite graph with p_c>0, almost surely every infinite component H of critical iid bond percolation has its own bond threshold p_c(H)=1.
assumptions: independent Bernoulli bond law at p_c

known_primary_attribution.role: known critical-cluster fragility mechanism; rederivation, no novelty

proof_or_counterexample: Independent thinning gives iid Bernoulli(p_c q), hence zero annealed survival for q<1. Nonnegative conditional survival is zero almost surely. Intersect over countably many vertices and rational q<1, then use monotonicity.
remaining_gap: This is a reduction, not absence of critical infinite components. The input ruling out maximally fragile iid critical components is unproved here.

exact_statement: Every infinite connected nearest-neighbor tree subgraph T of Z^d has p_c(T)=1. A comb spanning all vertices of Z^2 therefore has density one and p_c=1.
assumptions: T is connected, infinite and acyclic
independent q bond percolation on T
proof_or_counterexample: A tree has a unique root path to each endpoint. Length-n endpoints lie in the ambient box [-n,n]^d, giving at most (2n+1)^d paths. Their union probability is at most (2n+1)^d q^n, which tends to zero for q<1. The explicit comb retains all vertical bonds and horizontal bonds only at y=0.
remaining_gap: The comb is not quasi-transitive and not an iid lattice cluster. This refutes density-only robustness, not P0043.

exact_statement: For every d>=1 and integer R>=1 there is a translation-invariant site field on Z^d, with independence for sets at sup-norm distance greater than 2R+2, whose open probability is (2R-1)^d/((2R+1)^d+2d(2R+1)^(d-1)), but whose every open component has at most (2R+1)^d vertices. These probabilities tend to one as R tends to infinity.
assumptions: iid continuous labels on lattice sites
c(x) is the minimum-label site in the radius-R sup-norm box
x is open exactly when c(x) equals c(y) at all nearest neighbors y
proof_or_counterexample: Each open component has a common winner z and lies inside its radius-R box. Each site reads only radius R+1 labels. All minima agree exactly when the union minimum lies in the intersection; count the intersection and union. Exact finite controls are in MEASUREMENTS.json.
remaining_gap: No FKG, iid Bernoulli, insertion-tolerance or monotonicity property is asserted. This defeats only high-marginal plus unspecified finite-dependence deductions.

exact_statement: A downward-thinning proof needs to rule out maximally fragile infinite critical components under the iid Bernoulli law. Positive density and finite-event approximations do not by themselves provide a scale-compatible domination input epsilon<eta(k) when k depends on the approximation radius.
assumptions: block argument with dependence range k and error epsilon
proof_or_counterexample: Section 2 gives the conditional reduction; Sections 3 and 5 refute the generic replacement premises. Section 6 identifies the quantifier ordering needed for a block proof.
remaining_gap: An iid-specific scale-compatible local uniqueness or joint exploration theorem remains unproved here. The formulated robustness input is as strong as the target.

exact_statement: The published exponential-growth argument requires finite susceptibility below p_c and bounds the critical infimum two-point function by gr(G)^(-n); it does not require finite critical susceptibility. On the Delta-regular tree at p_c=1/(Delta-1), each sphere contributes Delta/(Delta-1) to susceptibility, so critical susceptibility is infinite.
assumptions: Delta>=3 integer for the tree example

source.locator: Theorem 1.3, Lemmas 1-2 and Theorem 2.5; independent tree computation in ATTEMPT.md section 7

proof_or_counterexample: The unique path to each sphere vertex has probability p_c^n. Multiplication by the sphere size gives Delta/(Delta-1) for every n, and summing diverges. For subexponential growth gr=1, the cited critical connectivity estimate is trivial.
remaining_gap: This corrects a mechanism description only and gives no bound for subexponential graphs.

exact_statement: On the D-regular tree, D>=3, set b=D-1 and c_b=(b-1)/(2b)*(1-1/b)^(b-2). For every n>=1 and 0<=p<=1/b, the derivative of the root-to-radius-n probability is at most D/c_b. For D=3 this is 12, tightening w432's valid bound 27 and extending its interval to all of [0,1/2].
assumptions: independent Bernoulli bond percolation on the D-regular tree

source.locator: section 8; separately derived from recurrence and open-pivotal witness identity

proof_or_counterexample: The forward survival bound is s_m<=1/(1+c_b*m). Open pivotals give p*s_m'<=m*s_m. Therefore f_n'<=D*(m+1)/(1+c_b*m)<=D/c_b, including p=0 by continuity. Exact constant calculations are in MEASUREMENTS.json.
